procedure.description: pembrolizumab injection, 200 mg, first-line therapy for metastatic non-small cell lung cancer

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Northwind Mutual Health denied the claim for HCPCS J9271 (pembrolizumab injection, 200 mg, first-line therapy for metastatic non-small cell lung cancer) with date of service 2026-04-18. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Pembrolizumab monotherapy is not indicated in the presence of an EGFR sensitizing mutation; first-line therapy for this member is an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor.

criteria.text: Histologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer that is metastatic (stage IV) or recurrent and not amenable to curative treatment.
PD-L1 tumor proportion score of 50 percent or greater for single-agent therapy (1 percent or greater when combined with platinum chemotherapy).
No EGFR sensitizing mutation and no ALK rearrangement, since targeted therapy is first-line for those tumors.
Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0 to 2.
No prior systemic therapy for metastatic disease.

chart.text: Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 209, LDL 157, HDL 39, triglycerides 97. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
Vitamin D came back 18. Started 1000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.
Work note requested for a sick day last Tuesday. Faxed to the employer.
Mammogram report forwarded for the record. Bilateral screening, BI-RADS 1, negative, routine screening in one year.

Referral letter from the primary care office. Thank you for seeing this patient of mine for evaluation. Her history and medication list are attached. Please let me know what you recommend and whether anything is needed from our end.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Patient called about a tick bite on the scalp after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 7 years.
Core needle biopsy, right upper lobe mass: adenocarcinoma, TTF-1 positive, napsin A positive, p40 negative. Consistent with primary lung adenocarcinoma.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
A1c came back 6.2. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.

Here with a cough and congestion for 9 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 13 and 18. No ocular pathology noted.

PET/CT: 5.3 centimeter hypermetabolic right upper lobe mass, hypermetabolic right hilar and subcarinal nodes, two hypermetabolic hepatic lesions in segments 6 and 7, and a lytic hypermetabolic lesion in the left iliac wing. Stage IV disease.

Mole on the upper back that her spouse noticed. About 7 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the right for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
PD-L1 immunohistochemistry (22C3): tumor proportion score 80 percent. Next-generation sequencing: EGFR exon 19 deletion detected. ALK, ROS1, BRAF, KRAS, MET, RET, NTRK negative.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the spring. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.

78 year old woman seen in medical oncology with her husband. Presented with three months of cough and 10 pounds of weight loss. Long discussion of goals: she wants treatment aimed at living longer and feeling well. Former smoker, 33 pack years, quit 10 years ago. Her history otherwise: seasonal allergies, mild asthma, albuterol maybe twice a year, hypothyroidism on levothyroxine. Allergies: sulfa, hives as a child. Never smoked, occasional beer, has three kids at home. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Stage IV lung adenocarcinoma with liver and bone metastases. Not a surgical or curative radiation candidate. ECOG 1. Still working part time, walks the dog every morning, some fatigue by evening and a cough. No prior systemic therapy. This is first-line treatment for metastatic disease.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 3 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.

Thoracic tumor board. Case presented. Consensus: single-agent immunotherapy first-line given the biomarker profile and performance status, palliative radiation to the iliac lesion if it becomes painful. Molecular results reviewed by the group.

Back to review the plan. Consented for pembrolizumab 200 milligrams every 3 weeks. Reviewed immune-related side effects, what to call about, and the port placement scheduled for later this week. Vitals today 138 over 74, pulse 79.
Infusion visit, cycle 1 day 1. Vitals stable, labs acceptable, pembrolizumab 200 milligrams intravenous over 30 minutes, tolerated without reaction. Return in 3 weeks.

expected.note: Plan exclusion: crit-3 (biomarker) cannot be met by any chart content.
